title: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) from the UK | Remote Workers
description: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) for remote workers and long stays for activities like Muay Thai or cooking courses. Who qualifies and how we apply.
intro: The Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) is a long-term, multiple-entry visa for remote workers and people taking part in activities such as Muay Thai, cooking or wellness courses in Thailand.

sections.heading: Who the Destination Thailand Visa is for
sections.text: The DTV suits digital nomads and remote workers employed or self-employed outside Thailand, and people staying for longer activities such as Muay Thai training, cooking courses or medical treatment. It allows long stays on each entry and multiple entries over several years.

sections.heading: What you need for a DTV
sections.text: You'll need proof of funds at the required level, and evidence of your remote work (such as an employment contract or company documents) or your activity (such as a booking with a Muay Thai camp or cooking school). You can't work for a Thai employer on a DTV.

sections.heading: Destination Thailand Visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and help travellers and businesses across the UK. We check the rules for your passport, prepare your application and keep you updated until it's decided.

sections.heading: Before you travel to Thailand
sections.text:
Check the UK government’s [travel advice for Thailand](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand) before you book, and again shortly before you go. It covers safety, local laws, health risks and the latest entry rules.

- Passport: most countries expect it to be valid for at least six months after you arrive, with blank pages for stamps. If yours is close to expiry, renew it first.
- Health: check the NHS fitfortravel website for Thailand at least eight weeks before you travel, in case you need vaccinations or malaria tablets. Some countries ask for a yellow fever certificate if you’ve recently been somewhere with yellow fever.
- Insurance: take out travel insurance that covers medical treatment and getting you home, and check it’s valid for Thailand.
- Bookings: carry copies of your return ticket and accommodation, as border officers can ask to see them.

We go through the entry requirements for your passport when we prepare your application, so you know exactly what to carry.

faqs.q: Can I work remotely in Thailand on a DTV?
faqs.a: Yes, for an employer or clients outside Thailand. You can’t work for a Thai company.

faqs.q: Do I need proof of funds?
faqs.a: Yes, at the level set by the Thai authorities. We confirm the current amount before you apply.

faqs.q: How long does a Destination Thailand Visa take?
faqs.a: Processing times vary with the authority and the time of year. Apply as early as you can, and don’t book non-refundable travel until your visa or authorisation is approved.

faqs.q: Can you help with my Destination Thailand Visa application?
faqs.a: Yes. We check which visa fits your trip, prepare your Destination Thailand Visa application and documents, and keep you updated. Contact us or call 0161 956 2003.
